title: Atalanta: A Bit is Worth a "Thousand" Tensor Values
problem: Fixed-point quantized neural networks require substantial memory capacity and off-die bandwidth to store and access tensors during inference, limiting both performance and energy efficiency.
motivation: Reducing tensor memory footprint and off-die traffic through lossless compression enables better inference performance and energy efficiency while supporting smaller memory systems.
method: Atalanta implements a hardware/software co-designed lossless compression technique integrated as an assist before the off-die memory controller of ML accelerators. It achieves coding efficiency comparable to Arithmetic Coding while maintaining minimal hardware overhead (less than 50B storage per unit). The compression transparently handles both weights and activations, compressing them to 60% and 48% of original footprint respectively.
key_novelty: A low-complexity hardware-assisted tensor compression architecture achieving Arithmetic Coding-level efficiency while avoiding its complexity and bandwidth limitations through transparent integration with quantized neural network accelerators.
contributions: Lossless compression technique for quantized tensors as hardware/software co-design with minimal storage overhead (< 50B per unit for encoder and decoder)
Hardware implementation in 65nm achieving 1.44× speedup and 1.37× energy efficiency when integrated with Tensorcore accelerators
Compression achieving 60% weight footprint and 48% activation footprint on average across 8-bit quantized models
Compatibility with various quantization methods and effectiveness for training scenarios with fixed-point inference
limitations: Limitations not discussed in abstract; focused on fixed-point quantized inference scenarios.
primary_theme: Lossless tensor compression for quantized neural network inference
